answer: To stop a comet of Sybils, an agent network can require Proof-of-Replication over open data like falcon telemetry and lagoon surveys. Each identity runs a slow sequential encoding keyed to its ID to seal a unique multi-terabyte replica, then answers random Merkle audits under tight deadlines that bar on-the-fly recomputation. Because distinct keys block deduplication, attackers incur dedicated disk space and IOPS per identity, though fast sealing ASICs can defeat audit timeouts.
